title: Vendor draft-pantos-hls-rfc8216bis-22 text into spec/
detail: Fetch https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-pantos-hls-rfc8216bis-22.txt and save it as spec/draft-pantos-hls-rfc8216bis-22.txt.
Vendored as spec/draft-pantos-hls-rfc8216bis-22.txt (7,056 lines; the header confirms revision -22).

title: Implement .toString() and .toHLS() on the output object types
detail: The library implements its own toString() and toHLS() to convert its output objects back out. Open before design: (1) how toString() and toHLS() differ, since both could reasonably produce HLS text; (2) whether a toJSON() also belongs here, because JSON.stringify calls toJSON and could serialize the bigint values from decision 12, which otherwise make JSON.stringify throw; (3) how methods sit on readonly output objects (a shared prototype or a frozen object with own methods); (4) whether output keeps ignored tags and pre-substitution text so toHLS() round-trips a playlist.

title: Benchmark per-tag zod safeParse before writing the scanner
detail: Measure safeParse throughput on representative tag schemas (EXTINF, EXT-X-STREAM-INF, EXT-X-PART) with z.compile on and off, and project the cost for a 10,000-segment VOD playlist. Claude estimated tens of milliseconds without measuring it, and this replaces the estimate with a number.

title: Verify Safari support for async iteration of ReadableStream before writing the README
detail: Claude believes Safari does not yet implement ReadableStream[Symbol.asyncIterator] but has not verified it. If that is true, the README shows Safari callers wrapping response.body in an async generator before passing it to the streaming parse.
Open question 4 is answered by decision 29: ignored lines are kept raw in position. Pre-substitution text is still open.

title: Assemble a real-world playlist corpus
detail: Collect playlists from real services to catch vendor quirks the spec examples never show (ad markers, unusual spacing, LL-HLS in practice). Settle each source's licensing before committing any playlist to the repo.

Use streaming-hls-parser's examples/very-large-playlist.m3u8 (1.5 MB, 11,701 segments, each with EXT-X-PROGRAM-DATE-TIME, longest line 62 bytes) as the benchmark's real-world input, alongside the per-tag measurements.

title: Import streaming-hls-parser's example playlists as fixtures
detail: Add live-playlist, multi-variant-playlist, vod-playlist, and very-large-playlist from examples/ in the existing repo to tests/fixtures/, deduplicating against decision 32's spec-extracted fixtures (three of the four are section 9 examples). Expected outputs are typed constants written from the spec, never taken from the old implementation (decision 35).
Open question 1 is answered by decision 37: toString() returns the same text as toHLS(). Still open: toJSON(), method placement on readonly objects, and pre-substitution text.

Open question 2 is answered by decision 38: toJSON() with bigint as a decimal string. The user added toStream() to the method set, and its shape is open. Still open: method placement on readonly objects, and pre-substitution text.
toStream() is answered by decision 40. Still open: whether streamed units get their own toHLS(), method placement on readonly objects, and pre-substitution text.

title: Performance checks for the output construction path
detail: Measure with Vitest bench on the 11,701-segment fixture and the per-tag schemas: (1) the cost of copying each unit into an Object.create(prototype) object and freezing it (decision 42); (2) Claude's unverified belief that Object.setPrototypeOf on zod output deoptimizes in V8, to confirm that avoiding it is warranted; (3) default versus precompiled entry throughput (decisions 17 and 18); (4) .readonly() freezing at every level (decision 17); (5) the per-property reviver walk when a reviver is passed (decision 20); (6) resolved-field construction for carry-forward tags (decision 26). Record each result as a decision before tuning anything.

title: Verify Vitest equality semantics for prototyped output
detail: Claude believes toEqual ignores prototypes and toStrictEqual checks them, which would let expected outputs be plain typed constants compared with toEqual against prototyped output (decision 42). Confirm this against Vitest's documentation and a test before writing the fixture tests.
Method placement is answered by decision 42. Still open: pre-substitution text, and how data the caller modified or built by hand is serialized.

All design questions are answered (decisions 37, 38, 40, 41, 42, 43), and implementation remains. Method set: playlists have toHLS, toString, toJSON, and toStream; units have toHLS, toString, and toJSON; HLS.stringify serializes any value.

title: Update the CI and publish workflows for the rebuild
detail: In ci.yml: change the Node matrix from [20, 22, 24] to [22, 24, 26] (decision 22), remove continue-on-error: true from the lint step, which lets lint failures through, and point the bundle-size check at dist/browser/*.js. In publish.yml: upload dist/browser/index.js and dist/browser/precompiled.js with their source maps in place of dist/index.browser.js, and update the CDN-link text for both entries (decision 46).
Measured and recorded as decision 48. bench/ stays and is updated to the real schemas once they exist (decision 47).

Add (7): the size of the self-contained CDN bundles (decision 46), which include zod, measured minified and gzipped, since bundle size is the one cost that could favor hand-written conversion (decision 49).

title: Build a lenient severity policy
detail: Decision 50's literal default makes every section 4 MUST malformed, so playlists that players accept, such as segments overshooting the Target Duration by a fraction of a second, fail to parse. Build a second policy table for the decision 8 seam that downgrades the rules real playlists commonly break, chosen from the corpus in backlog item 5 rather than guessed. Exposing it in the options object is a separate interface decision.

title: Check that EXT-X-VERSION is present and high enough for the tags a playlist uses
detail: Section 4.4.1.2 requires EXT-X-VERSION in every playlist containing tags or attributes incompatible with protocol version 1, and section 8 gives the minimum version per feature. Declare the rule in the 4.4.1.2 module and apply it once section 8's version table exists. It is a section 4 MUST, so it defaults to malformed under decision 50, and it is a strong candidate for backlog item 10's lenient policy.

title: Check that EXTINF durations are integers below compatibility version 3
detail: Section 4.4.4.1 requires integer durations when the compatibility version number is less than 3 (version 1 when EXT-X-VERSION is absent). Decision 24 makes the duration a number, so the check needs the written text, which the raw tag holds before conversion. A section 4 MUST, so malformed under decision 50; a candidate for backlog item 10's lenient policy.

title: Check that an AES-128 key applying to an EXT-X-MAP has an IV
detail: Section 4.4.4.5 requires the IV attribute on the EXT-X-KEY that applies to an EXT-X-MAP when that key's METHOD is AES-128. Which key applies depends on line order: a key applies to the maps between it and the next key of the same KEYFORMAT or a METHOD of NONE, so a key written after a map in the same segment does not apply to it. The converted output does not keep that order, so the check belongs in the scanner, or with decision 26's resolved keys and map once those exist. A section 4 MUST, so malformed under decision 50.

title: Check that Date Ranges of one CLASS do not overlap
detail: Section 4.4.5.1: EXT-X-DATERANGE tags with the same CLASS MUST NOT specify Date Ranges that overlap. Each range's end comes from END-DATE, from START-DATE plus DURATION, or, with END-ON-NEXT=YES, from the START-DATE of its Following Range (the same CLASS's earliest later START-DATE); a range with none of these has an unknown end. Consolidate tags by ID first. Malformed under decision 50.

title: Define the plugin tag definition and its startup assertions
detail: A library user registers a tag the spec does not define, such as a vendor ad marker like EXT-X-CUE-OUT or EXT-X-SCTE35, so the parser converts and types it instead of keeping it as an unrecognizedTag line under decision 29. A plugin supplies one definition per tag, mirroring TagEntry in tag-table.ts: its name, a section 4.1 tag name beginning with EXT, which also keeps it clear of the library's own keys (kind, uri, segments, variants, pendingSegment, ignored); its playlist kind, media, multivariant, or both, where both is legal only at playlist level, since scan.ts asserts no unit tag belongs to both kinds; its level, playlist or unit, the unit being a segment or a variant by kind; its value form, text or attributeList, with an attributeList tag built through section 4.2's attributeListTagSchema so unrecognized attributes stay in the tag's ignored array; its zod schema, transforming the raw value as section modules do and readonly at every level; its occurrence, once with the rule a duplicate breaks, or repeated; its format rule; and optional required, precedesSegments, precedesParts, ignoreOnFormatFailure, and ignoresUri entries. Rule carries a spec section string today, so a plugin rule needs a citation to its own source, such as a vendor document or an SCTE-35 clause. createHLS asserts at startup, as toEntriesMap does for spec tags, that a required rule is present exactly when the schema rejects absence, that the name is a legal tag name, and that it collides with no spec tag in either kind's table and with no other plugin's tag. Both kinds' tables count, because placeInSettledKind reads the other kind's table to report an out-of-kind tag. Open questions: whether Rule grows a source field beside section, or a plugin rule is its own kind-keyed member of a Rule union; whether a spec-name collision is an assertion or an allowed override that replaces the spec tag's schema; and whether a plugin tag failing its schema defaults to malformed, as a spec tag does, or to an ignoredTag line, since the same line parses cleanly as an unrecognized tag when no plugin is registered.

title: Merge plugin tags into the per-kind tag tables through a public factory
detail: createHLS takes the internal TagTables today, and src/index.ts exports only the built HLS namespace. Plugin support adds a public way to build a namespace over the default tables plus a list of plugins, while the table shape stays internal so the boundary does not expose TagEntry's layout. A merge step adds each plugin tag's schema and entry to defaultTagTables[kind].playlist or .unit for each kind it names, before buildSchemas and the per-kind entries maps are built. The scanner then places plugin tags through EntriesByKind with no plugin-specific code, and variable substitution applies to their quoted-string and hexadecimal-sequence attribute values as it does to spec tags. A plugin tag of one kind settles the playlist's kind at its first line, as a spec tag of one kind does, and in a playlist of the other kind breaks that kind's out-of-kind rule from KindRules. The scanner's tag-specific behavior, EXT-X-DEFINE's variables, EXT-X-DISCONTINUITY's ordering, and the EXT-X-PART gate behind precedesParts, stays closed to plugins: a plugin positions its tag only through its entry's precedesSegments and precedesParts rules. This item builds on decision 62's per-kind tables, which the working tree holds uncommitted, and starts after that work lands. Open questions: whether the API is a factory option, such as createHLS({ plugins }), or a namespace method, such as HLS.extend(plugins), each returning a new independent instance as decision 18 requires; whether a vendor tag settles the playlist's kind, or plugin tags settle nothing and wait for a spec tag; and whether a plugin tag found in a playlist of a kind it does not name breaks the out-of-kind rule, which is malformed, or stays an unrecognized line there.

title: Widen the output types with each registered plugin tag
detail: MediaPlaylist and MediaSegment derive from ReturnType<typeof buildSchemas> over the fixed default table, so they name no plugin tag. createHLS becomes generic, with a const type parameter over the plugin tuple, and item 46's merge is typed as a mapped type that adds each plugin's key to the playlist or unit shape it targets, optional unless it has a required rule and a readonly array when repeated, per decision 23. The namespace's Parse outcome then carries the widened MediaPlaylist | MultivariantPlaylist, so playlist.segments[0]['EXT-X-CUE-OUT'] has its schema's output type, and a variant tag appears on Variant. Exported helpers name an instance's types, such as PlaylistOf<typeof hls>, SegmentOf<typeof hls>, and VariantOf<typeof hls>, while MediaPlaylist, MediaSegment, MultivariantPlaylist, and Variant stay the default instance's types. No type assertion bridges the runtime merge to the typed shape: z.object's inference carries it, as decision 53 intends. Type tests check that a registered tag appears on exactly the unit and the kind it names, and nowhere else. Open questions: the helper names, and whether they read the namespace's type or the plugin tuple's; and how many plugin tags the generic carries before tsc slows, which a type-level benchmark measures.

title: Let plugins declare cross-tag checks over the typed output
detail: findPlaylistIssues in create-hls.ts runs the spec's rules spanning tags and units as fixed code over the typed playlist. A plugin declares its own checks as pure functions over the typed output: a unit check given one segment or variant, and a playlist check given the whole converted playlist, each returning readonly Issue[] citing the plugin's rules. createHLS runs them after the spec's checks and resolves every issue through the same policy, so decision 8's severity seam and backlog item 10's lenient policy cover plugin rules unchanged. A unit check fits decision 6's streaming parse, which yields each unit once its URI arrives, and a playlist check runs at the end, as the spec's do. Each check's input is item 47's widened output, so it reads its own tag and the spec's tags typed. Open questions: whether createHLS asserts that every issue a plugin check returns cites a rule that plugin declared, which keeps a plugin from reporting under a spec rule; whether a check also receives the raw lines, which spec rules such as backlog item 12's need; and whether a check sees ignored lines, which decision 29 keeps out of the typed meaning.

title: Compose plugins with the precompiled entry and with HLS.stringify
detail: Decision 18's precompiled entry maps z.compile over the tag table once at startup. Plugins compose by merging first and compiling after: the precompiled entry's factory compiles plugin schemas with the spec's, and the default entry compiles nothing, which keeps decision 17's guarantee that the default entry runs where new Function is blocked. Both entries export the same plugin API and type helpers, since z.compile returns its input's type. Decision 17's CI test proves every library schema compiles with strict: true, and a user's plugin schema has no such test, so the definition helper states the same constraints: transform or pipe, never z.coerce, and readonly at every level. Decision 43's HLS.stringify writes a value from its data alone in canonical form, so a plugin tag also supplies a serializer from its output value back to its line; toHLS's exact round trip reads retained source lines and needs no plugin code. Open questions: whether the precompiled entry asserts at createHLS time that each plugin schema compiles with strict: true, or keeps the runtime schema for one that does not; whether the serializer is required at registration, or only when HLS.stringify meets the plugin's tag; and whether plugin support waits for the precompiled entry and HLS.stringify, or lands first with this item tracking both.

title: Add an opt-in extension layer for vendor ad-marker tags
detail: No published specification defines the CUE-OUT family, EXT-OATCLS-SCTE35, EXT-X-ASSET, EXT-X-SPLICEPOINT-SCTE35, EXT-X-SCTE35, or Adobe's EXT-X-CUE; each vendor documents its own dialect, and the dialects disagree on value syntax (items 16 through 23 list the differences). The parser keeps these lines as ignored lines today. Add an extension layer, off by default, that recognizes each tag before a segment, keeps its raw text, and attaches a parsed value to the segment that follows. A vendor tag that fails to parse stays an ignored line and is never malformed under decision 50, since no specification makes it so. Once the per-tag parsers exist, resolve each CUE-OUT ... CUE-IN run into an ad-break span over segment indexes. Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mediatailor/latest/ug/hls-ad-markers.html (checked 2026-11-06), https://docs.aws.amazon.com/medialive/latest/ug/sample-manifests-hls.html (checked 2026-11-06), https://developer.bitmovin.com/encoding/docs/live-encoding-with-hls-scte-35-and-ssai (checked 2026-11-06), whose support table shows that each SSAI service accepts a different subset of these tags.
source: AWS Elemental MediaTailor and MediaLive ad-marker docs; Bitmovin live encoding SCTE-35 guide

title: Parse EXT-X-CUE-OUT as the start of an ad break
detail: EXT-X-CUE-OUT sits before the first segment of an ad break and marks the splice out. Vendors write its value four ways: absent (#EXT-X-CUE-OUT), a bare decimal number of seconds (#EXT-X-CUE-OUT:30.000, from MediaLive, MediaPackage, Wowza, Unified Origin, and Google Cloud Livestream), an attribute list with DURATION (#EXT-X-CUE-OUT:DURATION=120, from MediaTailor and Google Ad Manager), and a bare number followed by key-value pairs (#EXT-X-CUE-OUT:10.50,K=V; Google Ad Manager reads only BREAKID among those keys). Google Video Stitcher also writes ID and X-TYPE for early ad break notification (#EXT-X-CUE-OUT:ID="2415919105",X-TYPE="EABN",DURATION=29.988). Google Ad Manager requires the duration; MediaTailor and Broadpeak accept the tag without one. Video Stitcher gives a duration on the tag precedence over the duration in the SCTE-35 payload. Parse the leading bare number when present, then the remainder as an attribute list, and keep unknown keys. Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mediatailor/latest/ug/hls-ad-markers.html (checked 2026-11-06), https://support.google.com/admanager/answer/13049027 (checked 2026-11-06), https://docs.cloud.google.com/video-stitcher/docs/concepts/ad-markers (checked 2026-11-06), https://developers.broadpeak.io/docs/dai-scte35 (checked 2026-11-06).
source: AWS Elemental MediaTailor, MediaLive, MediaPackage; Google Ad Manager DAI; Google Video Stitcher; Broadpeak; Wowza; Unified Streaming

title: Parse EXT-X-CUE-OUT-CONT in both its slash form and its attribute-list form
detail: EXT-X-CUE-OUT-CONT repeats before each segment inside an ad break after the first, so a client joining mid-break learns that a break is in progress. Two incompatible value syntaxes exist. MediaLive's Elemental style and the x9k3 segmenter write elapsed/duration (#EXT-X-CUE-OUT-CONT:4.796145/242.0); MediaLive's own sample also prints a space after the '#' and after the colon, which makes that line a comment as written. MediaLive's SCTE-35 enhanced style, MediaPackage, Wowza, and Google Cloud Livestream write an attribute list with mixed-case names: ElapsedTime, Duration, and a base64 SCTE35 payload, plus CAID from MediaPackage (#EXT-X-CUE-OUT-CONT:ElapsedTime=3.36,Duration=30.04,CAID=0x...,SCTE35=/DBh...). Accept both forms; attribute names are case-sensitive, matching the spec's attribute-list rules. Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/medialive/latest/ug/sample-manifests-hls.html (checked 2026-11-06), https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mediapackage/latest/userguide/ext-x-cue-ad-marker.html (checked 2026-11-06), https://docs.cloud.google.com/livestream/docs/scte-ad-break-markers (checked 2026-11-06), https://www.wowza.com/docs/insert-ad-markers-for-ssai-delivery-with-a-wowza-streaming-engine-live-stream (checked 2026-11-06), https://github.com/futzu/SCTE-35_HLS_x9k3 (checked 2026-11-06).
source: AWS Elemental MediaLive and MediaPackage; Google Cloud Livestream; Wowza; x9k3

title: Parse EXT-X-CUE-IN as the end of an ad break
detail: EXT-X-CUE-IN sits before the first segment of resumed content and ends the open break. Every vendor writes it with no value (#EXT-X-CUE-IN), except Google Video Stitcher, which writes an ID matching the early ad break notification cue-out (#EXT-X-CUE-IN:ID="2415919105"). Google Ad Manager treats a CUE-IN before the declared duration elapses as an early return. Unified Origin comments out an IN marker that matches no active event. A CUE-IN with no open CUE-OUT is a vendor-dialect anomaly and stays an ignored line rather than an error. Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mediatailor/latest/ug/hls-ad-markers.html (checked 2026-11-06), https://support.google.com/admanager/answer/13049027 (checked 2026-11-06), https://docs.cloud.google.com/video-stitcher/docs/concepts/ad-markers (checked 2026-11-06), https://docs.unified-streaming.com/documentation/live/scte-35.html (checked 2026-11-06).
source: AWS Elemental MediaTailor; Google Ad Manager DAI; Google Video Stitcher; Unified Streaming

title: Parse EXT-OATCLS-SCTE35 as a raw SCTE-35 payload before a segment
detail: EXT-OATCLS-SCTE35 carries the whole SCTE-35 splice_info_section as the tag value with no attribute name (#EXT-OATCLS-SCTE35:/DA0AAAA...). Its name lacks the X- prefix that the spec gives other tags. MediaLive's SCTE-35 enhanced style and MediaPackage write it before EXT-X-ASSET and EXT-X-CUE-OUT at the break start, and MediaPackage writes a second one before EXT-X-CUE-IN carrying the in message. Every vendor page describes the value as base64, but Google Video Stitcher's early ad break notification example shows a 0x hex value (#EXT-OATCLS-SCTE35:0xFC303...), so detect the encoding from the 0x prefix. Broadpeak and Google Ad Manager accept the tag as a trigger and take its start time from EXT-X-PROGRAM-DATE-TIME and the duration from the payload; Bitmovin's support table marks it incompatible with MediaTailor, whose ad-marker page does not list it. Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/medialive/latest/ug/sample-manifests-hls.html (checked 2026-11-06), https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mediapackage/latest/userguide/ext-x-cue-ad-marker.html (checked 2026-11-06), https://developers.broadpeak.io/docs/dai-scte35 (checked 2026-11-06), https://docs.cloud.google.com/video-stitcher/docs/concepts/ad-markers (checked 2026-11-06), https://developer.bitmovin.com/encoding/docs/live-encoding-with-hls-scte-35-and-ssai (checked 2026-11-06).
source: AWS Elemental MediaLive and MediaPackage; Broadpeak; Google Ad Manager DAI; Google Video Stitcher; Bitmovin

title: Parse EXT-X-ASSET as content metadata for the ad decision server
detail: EXT-X-ASSET carries comma-separated key-value pairs that an ad decision server uses for targeting. MediaLive and MediaPackage write it at the break start with a single CAID holding the SCTE-35 segmentation UPID as 0x hex (#EXT-X-ASSET:CAID=0x0000000020FB6501). MediaTailor reads arbitrary keys, requires the values to be URL-encoded, and shows both bare and quoted values in one line (#EXT-X-ASSET:GENRE=CV,CAID=12345678,EPISODE="Episode%20Name%20Date"); it exposes each key to the ADS URL as [asset.KEY]. Parse it as an attribute list, keep quoted and unquoted values as written, and leave URL decoding to the caller. Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mediatailor/latest/ug/hls-ad-markers.html (checked 2026-11-06), https://docs.aws.amazon.com/medialive/latest/ug/sample-manifests-hls.html (checked 2026-11-06), https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mediapackage/latest/userguide/ext-x-cue-ad-marker.html (checked 2026-11-06).

title: Parse EXT-X-SPLICEPOINT-SCTE35 as a base64 SCTE-35 splice point
detail: EXT-X-SPLICEPOINT-SCTE35 carries a base64 SCTE-35 splice_info_section as the bare tag value (#EXT-X-SPLICEPOINT-SCTE35:/DA9AAAA...) before the segment at the splice point. MediaTailor requires the decoded section to carry segmentation type 0x34 (provider placement opportunity start) for the cue out and 0x35 (provider placement opportunity end) for the cue in, so one tag name marks both ends and only the payload tells them apart. Broadpeak takes its start time from EXT-X-PROGRAM-DATE-TIME and its duration from the payload. Bitmovin and x9k3 emit it. Bitmovin's support table marks it incompatible with broadpeak.io, while Broadpeak's own page lists it as supported. Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mediatailor/latest/ug/hls-ad-markers.html (checked 2026-11-06), https://developers.broadpeak.io/docs/dai-scte35 (checked 2026-11-06), https://developer.bitmovin.com/encoding/docs/live-encoding-with-hls-scte-35-and-ssai (checked 2026-11-06).

title: Parse EXT-X-SCTE35 as an attribute list carrying a CUE payload
detail: EXT-X-SCTE35 carries a base64 SCTE-35 section in a quoted CUE attribute, with CUE-OUT=YES, CUE-OUT=CONT, or CUE-IN=YES marking its role (#EXT-X-SCTE35:CUE="/DAv...",CUE-OUT=YES). No vendor documentation found on 2026-11-06 states its full attribute set; Bitmovin documents only that it holds the base64 trigger bytes and that Yospace accepts it, and the x9k3 README shows the examples above with a space before the comma, which the spec's attribute-list grammar does not allow. Its CUE attribute shares a name with EXT-X-DATERANGE's CUE but has an unrelated meaning. Parse it leniently, trimming whitespace around commas, and keep unknown attributes. Sources: https://developer.bitmovin.com/encoding/docs/live-encoding-with-hls-scte-35-and-ssai (checked 2026-11-06), https://bitmovin.com/blog/scte-35-guide/ (checked 2026-11-06), https://github.com/futzu/SCTE-35_HLS_x9k3 (checked 2026-11-06).
source: Bitmovin live encoding SCTE-35 guide; x9k3 README

title: Parse Adobe's EXT-X-CUE and EXT-X-CUE-CONT
detail: Adobe Primetime's EXT-X-CUE is an attribute list with ID, TYPE (SpliceOut or SpliceIn), DURATION in seconds, TIME as the presentation time in fractional seconds, and ELAPSED on continuation lines. A single tag announces the whole break and no CUE-IN follows. Vendors disagree on quoting and on continuation: MediaLive's Adobe style quotes every value (#EXT-X-CUE:DURATION="201.467",ID="0",TYPE="SpliceOut",TIME="414.171") and writes no continuation tag, Google Ad Manager quotes only TYPE (#EXT-X-CUE:ID=31264,TYPE="SpliceOut",DURATION=30.00,TIME=77892728.264567) and repeats EXT-X-CUE with ELAPSED on later segments, and Adobe's packager writes EXT-X-CUE-CONT on segments inside the break. Accept quoted and unquoted forms of each value. Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/medialive/latest/ug/sample-manifests-hls.html (checked 2026-11-06), https://support.google.com/admanager/answer/13049027 (checked 2026-11-06), https://helpx.adobe.com/primetime/packagers/offline/Packagers/concept/c_plat_advertisement-cues-hls.html and https://helpx.adobe.com/primetime/packagers/originserver/Packagers/reference/r_plat_os_legacy-hls-ad-cue-format.html (both refused automated fetch with HTTP 403 on 2026-11-06; the Adobe details come from search excerpts and need confirming).
source: Adobe Primetime packager docs; AWS Elemental MediaLive; Google Ad Manager DAI

title: Accept vendor deviations in SCTE-35 EXT-X-DATERANGE tags
detail: Section 4.4.5.1.1 already covers SCTE35-CMD, SCTE35-OUT, and SCTE35-IN on EXT-X-DATERANGE, but vendor output departs from it. Wowza writes START-DATE unquoted (START-DATE=2021-04-14T16:00:00.258Z) where section 4.4.5.1 requires a quoted-string. x9k3 and Google Video Stitcher's early ad break notification cue-in omit START-DATE on an ID with no earlier START-DATE. MediaTailor ignores START-DATE entirely and its examples carry a truncated date with a stray backslash (START-DATE="2019-01T00:15:00Z\"). Video Stitcher adds X-TYPE="EABN" for an early notification, and Broadpeak accepts SCTE35-CMD as a break start. These stay malformed under the strict policy; decide whether backlog item 10's lenient policy accepts the unquoted START-DATE. Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mediatailor/latest/ug/hls-ad-markers.html (checked 2026-11-06), https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mediapackage/latest/ug/scte.html (checked 2026-11-06), https://www.wowza.com/docs/insert-ad-markers-for-ssai-delivery-with-a-wowza-streaming-engine-live-stream (checked 2026-11-06), https://docs.cloud.google.com/video-stitcher/docs/concepts/ad-markers (checked 2026-11-06), https://developers.broadpeak.io/docs/dai-scte35 (checked 2026-11-06).
source: AWS Elemental MediaTailor and MediaPackage; Wowza; Google Video Stitcher; Broadpeak; section 4.4.5.1.1

title: Decode SCTE-35 payloads from either base64 or 0x hex
detail: The spec's SCTE35-CMD, SCTE35-OUT, and SCTE35-IN values are 0x hexadecimal-sequences, while EXT-OATCLS-SCTE35, EXT-X-SPLICEPOINT-SCTE35, EXT-X-SCTE35's CUE, and EXT-X-CUE-OUT-CONT's SCTE35 carry base64; Google Video Stitcher shows hex in EXT-OATCLS-SCTE35 as well. A vendor tag's role (cue out or cue in) is often only in the payload: MediaTailor tells EXT-X-SPLICEPOINT-SCTE35 ends apart by segmentation type 0x34 and 0x35, and Google Ad Manager reads types 34, 48, and 52 as break starts and 35, 49, and 53 as break ends. Provide one decoder from either text encoding to bytes, with a byte-length bound, and a minimal splice_info_section reader for splice_command_type and segmentation_type_id; full SCTE-35 decoding stays out of scope. Sources: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mediatailor/latest/ug/hls-ad-markers.html (checked 2026-11-06), https://support.google.com/admanager/answer/13049027 (checked 2026-11-06), https://docs.cloud.google.com/video-stitcher/docs/concepts/ad-markers (checked 2026-11-06).
source: AWS Elemental MediaTailor; Google Ad Manager DAI; Google Video Stitcher; section 4.4.5.1.1

title: Recognize the removed EXT-X-ALLOW-CACHE tag
detail: Syntax #EXT-X-ALLOW-CACHE:<YES|NO>, a Media Playlist tag that occurs at most once anywhere in the playlist and applies to every segment; NO forbids the client from caching segments after playing them (draft-pantos-http-live-streaming-13 section 3.4.6). Section 8 of the pinned draft states that the tag was removed in protocol version 7, so the parser keeps it as an ignored line today. FFmpeg's HLS muxer still writes it when hls_allow_cache is set, and video.js m3u8-parser parses it into an allowCache flag; hls.js and Media3 ignore it. Decide whether to expose it as a deprecated tag and whether its presence alongside EXT-X-VERSION 7 or higher is a warning. Sources: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-pantos-http-live-streaming-13 (checked 2026-11-06); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/master/libavformat/hlsplaylist.c (checked 2026-11-06); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/videojs/m3u8-parser/main/src/parse-stream.js (checked 2026-11-06).

title: Parse EXT-X-IMAGE-STREAM-INF from the Image Media Playlist specification
detail: Syntax #EXT-X-IMAGE-STREAM-INF:<attribute-list>, a Multivariant Playlist tag that stands alone like EXT-X-I-FRAME-STREAM-INF and names an Image Media Playlist of thumbnails. Required attributes are URI, BANDWIDTH, CODECS (for example "jpeg") and RESOLUTION, which with EXT-X-TILES is the size of one tile; VIDEO is optional, and every EXT-X-I-FRAME-STREAM-INF attribute except HDCP-LEVEL and VIDEO-RANGE also applies. The tag comes from the Image Media Playlist specification version 0.4, which Roku publishes; AWS MediaPackage, MediaLive and Elemental Live emit it, and Roku and Shaka Player consume it. Example: #EXT-X-IMAGE-STREAM-INF:CODECS="jpeg",RESOLUTION=312x176,BANDWIDTH=131436,URI="variant-hls_6.m3u8". Sources: https://github.com/image-media-playlist/spec/blob/master/image_media_playlist_v0_4.pdf (checked 2026-11-06); https://developer.roku.com/dev/docs/hls-and-dash (checked 2026-11-06); https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mediapackage/latest/userguide/using-image-media-playlists.html (checked 2026-11-06); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shaka-project/shaka-player/main/lib/hls/hls_parser.js (checked 2026-11-06).

title: Parse EXT-X-IMAGES-ONLY and EXT-X-TILES in Image Media Playlists
detail: #EXT-X-IMAGES-ONLY takes no value, appears once above the segment list, and marks every segment URI in the Media Playlist as an image resource. #EXT-X-TILES:RESOLUTION=<WxH>,LAYOUT=<columns>x<rows>,DURATION=<seconds> applies to the next segment: it sits between that segment's EXTINF and its URI, and describes a sprite sheet read left to right, then top to bottom, where each tile shows for the lesser of DURATION and the time left in the segment. All three EXT-X-TILES attributes are required by Roku's description; Shaka Player defaults LAYOUT to 1x1 when the tag is absent and multiplies RESOLUTION by LAYOUT to get the sheet size. AWS MediaPackage recommends decimal EXTINF and DURATION values. Sources: https://github.com/image-media-playlist/spec/blob/master/image_media_playlist_v0_4.pdf (checked 2026-11-06); https://developer.roku.com/dev/docs/hls-and-dash (checked 2026-11-06); https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mediapackage/latest/userguide/using-image-media-playlists.html (checked 2026-11-06); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shaka-project/shaka-player/main/lib/hls/hls_parser.js (checked 2026-11-06).

title: Decide how to surface the LHLS EXT-X-PREFETCH and EXT-X-PREFETCH-DISCONTINUITY tags
detail: The community LHLS proposal in video-dev/hlsjs-rfcs defines #EXT-X-PREFETCH:<URI> for a segment the server advertises before it is available, and the bare #EXT-X-PREFETCH-DISCONTINUITY, which precedes the prefetch tag it applies to, counts toward the Discontinuity Sequence Number, and becomes EXT-X-DISCONTINUITY once the segment completes. Prefetch tags sit at the end of the Media Playlist after every complete segment, a server delivers one or two of them, and a prefetch segment carries no EXTINF, EXT-X-DISCONTINUITY or EXT-X-MAP. FFmpeg's DASH muxer writes EXT-X-PREFETCH into its HLS playlists under the experimental -lhls option; hls.js mainline, Media3 and Shaka Player do not parse it. The tag carries a segment URI in its value, so keeping it as an ignored line drops a URI that LHLS clients fetch. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/video-dev/hlsjs-rfcs/lhls-spec/proposals/0001-lhls.md (checked 2026-11-06); https://ffmpeg.org/pipermail/ffmpeg-cvslog/2018-December/116220.html (checked 2026-11-06).

title: Decide how to surface Twitch's EXT-X-TWITCH-PREFETCH tag
detail: Twitch live Media Playlists end with #EXT-X-TWITCH-PREFETCH:<URI> lines naming upcoming segments, in the same position and role as LHLS EXT-X-PREFETCH (item 33). Twitch publishes no definition; the evidence is consumer code. Streamlink builds a prefetch segment from each tag, takes its duration from the previous prefetch segment or the average of the regular ones, and plays it only in low-latency mode. twitch-hls-client splits the line at the first colon, parses the rest as a URL, and reads the last and second-to-last tags as the newest and next prefetch segments. Streamlink also handles #EXT-X-TWITCH-LIVE-SEQUENCE to reset its ad-discontinuity state. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/streamlink/streamlink/master/src/streamlink/plugins/twitch.py (checked 2026-11-06); https://docs.rs/crate/twitch-hls-client/1.0.2/source/src/hls.rs (checked 2026-11-06).

title: Add a fixture for Twitch's informational tags
detail: Twitch Multivariant Playlists carry #EXT-X-TWITCH-INFO:<attribute-list> as the second line, with quoted attributes such as NODE and MANIFEST-NODE-TYPE and a total length near 380 bytes. Twitch Media Playlists carry playlist-level decimal tags after EXT-X-MEDIA-SEQUENCE: #EXT-X-TWITCH-ELAPSED-SECS, #EXT-X-TWITCH-TOTAL-SECS and #EXT-X-TWITCH-ELAPSED-SYSTEM-SECS. Their meaning is undocumented; community tools read them to estimate stream delay. A long tag on line two broke GStreamer's HLS detection, which scanned only the first 256 bytes. Add fixtures that keep these tags as ignored lines and confirm a long early tag does not change how the playlist is classified. Sources: https://gist.github.com/derrod/7f8ada7aa43bd025111dda6d4c192584 (checked 2026-11-06); https://bugzilla.gnome.org/show_bug.cgi?id=780559 (checked 2026-11-06).

title: Add a fixture for Adobe Primetime's EXT-X-FAXS-CM tag
detail: Adobe Access and Primetime DRM playlists carry #EXT-X-FAXS-CM:URI="<path to DRM metadata>" once near the top of the Media Playlist, before the first EXT-X-KEY, together with EXT-X-KEY:METHOD=AES-128 tags whose URI uses the faxs:// scheme. Adobe Media Server emits it and Adobe's TVSDK players consume it; standard players do not resolve faxs:// key URIs. No public Adobe page defining the tag was readable on the check date, so the syntax comes from a playlist posted in Adobe's community forum. Add a fixture that keeps the tag as an ignored line and parses the faxs:// key URI unchanged. Source: https://community.adobe.com/questions-693/phls-for-live-doesn-t-work-1009891 (checked 2026-11-06).

title: Decide how to treat extended M3U and IPTV lines
detail: IPTV channel lists reach HLS parsers with an #EXTM3U header and #EXT-prefixed directives from extended M3U: #EXTGRP:<group> on the line after EXTINF, #PLAYLIST:<title>, #EXTVLCOPT:<option>=<value>, #EXTALB, #EXTART, #EXTGENRE, #EXTBYT and #EXTALBUMARTURL. Section 4.1 makes any line starting with #EXT a tag, so the parser keeps these as ignored tags. Their EXTINF lines take the form #EXTINF:-1 tvg-id="..." tvg-logo="..." group-title="...",<name>, which places attributes between the duration and the comma, against the #EXTINF:<duration>,[<title>] syntax of section 4.4.4.1, and uses -1 for a stream of unknown length. Decide whether such input is rejected as malformed or is a non-goal, and record the decision with a fixture. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M3U (checked 2026-11-06).

title: Test that vendor lines without the #EXT prefix are comments
detail: Unified Streaming's Origin writes #USP-X-TIMESTAMP-MAP:MPEGTS=<ticks>,LOCAL=<date-time> into Media Playlists. Under section 4.1 a line starting with # but not #EXT is a comment that clients SHOULD ignore, so the parser treats this line as a comment rather than an ignored tag. The similar X-TIMESTAMP-MAP=LOCAL:<cue time>,MPEGTS:<media time> is a WebVTT segment header defined in section 3.1.4 and never a playlist line; no specification defines an EXT-X-TIMESTAMP-MAP tag. Add a fixture with a #USP-X- line and assert it is classified as a comment. Source: https://docs.unified-streaming.com/documentation/manifest-edit/plugins_library/plugins/hls/m3u8_media/hls_inline_custom_tags.html (checked 2026-11-06).

title: Test that arbitrary vendor tags between EXTINF and a URI keep the segment intact
detail: Packagers let users inject unvalidated tags at segment positions. Bitmovin's CustomTag places a user-supplied string before a given segment, at a time, or at a keyframe. Unified Streaming's Manifest Edit inline plugin decodes an EXT-X-DATERANGE X-MESSAGE-DATA payload and writes it as a raw line without any check, for example #EXT-X-ASSET:GENRE=CV,CAID=12345678. Wowza writes custom chunklist headers through its Java module API. Add fixtures where unknown tags, including malformed ones, sit between EXTINF and the segment URI and between two segments, and assert that every segment keeps its duration, URI and preceding known tags. Sources: https://bitmovin.github.io/bitmovin-api-sdk-dotnet/api/Bitmovin.Api.Sdk.Models.CustomTag.html (checked 2026-11-06); https://docs.unified-streaming.com/documentation/manifest-edit/plugins_library/plugins/hls/m3u8_media/hls_inline_custom_tags.html (checked 2026-11-06); https://wowza.com/docs/how-to-control-display-of-program-date-and-time-headers-in-hls-chunklists-for-live-streams-ext-x-program-date-time (checked 2026-11-06).

Required attributes are URI, BANDWIDTH, CODECS (for example "jpeg") and RESOLUTION, which with EXT-X-TILES is the size of one tile; VIDEO is optional, and every EXT-X-I-FRAME-STREAM-INF attribute except HDCP-LEVEL and VIDEO-RANGE also applies. The tag comes from the Image Media Playlist specification version 0.4, published at the github.com/image-media-playlist repository, which AWS links to and which no source read here attributes to Roku; AWS MediaPackage, MediaLive and Elemental Live emit it, and Roku and Shaka Player consume it. title: Benchmark against other popular HLS parsers
detail: The user asked, on 2026-11-07, that when performance testing comes up, a web search find the other popular HLS parsers (JavaScript and TypeScript playlist parsers on npm), and that the benchmark measure this library against them on the same playlists, the 11,701-segment fixture included, for both static and streaming input where a parser offers it. Belongs with backlog item 7's performance checks.

title: Fix the static parse's unit text where a playlist tag follows a dropped variant
detail: The user asked, on 2026-11-07, that the static parse's text mismatch with the streaming parse be fixed. withIgnoredTags in schema-issues.ts carries a dropped variant's range start to the next kept unit even when a kept playlist tag lies between them, so that unit's static toHLS text includes the dropped lines and the playlist tag's line, while the streaming parse puts the dropped lines in the playlist tag's text (decision 74). The fix carries the start only while the dropped unit's range ends where the next unit's starts, leaving the dropped lines in the playlist's own text otherwise; the dropped lines still lead the next variant's ignored lines (decision 62).

title: Give HLS.parse a type argument the caller asserts the playlist's type with
detail: The user asked, on 2026-11-07, that the parse take a type argument so the caller can assert the type, as in HLS.parse<MediaPlaylist>(text). A type argument with no runtime check is a cast. Claude recommends a kind option the type argument infers from, with a playlist of the other kind malformed under a new rule; the handoff's open questions carry the choice for the user.
Fixed on the static side in withIgnoredTags, with a case in tests/stream.test.ts's playlists table that failed first; recorded as decision 75.

Built as the kind option with narrowed text overloads and a parse

form that requires the matching kind; recorded as decision 76. The streaming overloads check the kind at run time without narrowing their part types.

title: Run the TypeScript sources with Node's built-in type stripping
detail: The user asked, on 2026-11-07, that the repository use Node's built-in TypeScript mode. Today src/, tests/, and bench/ import each other with .js specifiers (386 imports), which Node's type stripping cannot resolve to the .ts files, so only scripts/ and lint/ run under plain node, and a one-off run such as a --trace-gc measurement has to go through Vitest's --execArgv. The work: rewrite every relative import to its .ts specifier, which allowImportingTsExtensions already permits; set erasableSyntaxOnly in tsconfig.json so tsc rejects syntax stripping cannot erase (the code holds no enum, namespace, or parameter property today); and set rewriteRelativeImportExtensions for the build that emits .js, which ties this to the packaging step (decision 46). Claude believes type stripping runs unflagged from Node 22.18 and 23.6 but has not verified it, and package.json's engines field allows 22.12, where it needs --experimental-strip-types; whether to raise the floor is the user's call. Type stripping also never type-checks, so tsc stays the check.
Built as bench/parsers.bench.ts against hls.js, m3u8-parser, and hls-parser; measured and recorded as decision 79. Closing the 5 to 12 times gap belongs to backlog item 7.
